themes_detail.label: Sewer System Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints have spiked to 14 THIS WEEK—more than triple the 4.4-complaint weekly average—signaling a potential infrastructure failure or blockage affecting Coney Island/Brighton Beach residents.
evidence: 14 sewer complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (220% increase, z-score: 5.57)
Spike is acute and current, not historical—demands immediate investigation
Related spike: Root/Sewer/Sidewalk Condition complaints up 700% (3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 avg), suggesting cascading infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Interview DEP on what triggered the surge—is there a known blockage, main break, or wet weather event?
Canvass residents in areas with concentrated complaints for health/sanitation impacts and duration
Cross-check against DEP work orders and maintenance schedules filed this week

themes_detail.label: Garbage Collection Backlog Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Missed collection complaints jumped to 9 THIS WEEK—4.5x the 2.0-complaint weekly baseline—suggesting DSNY collection failures or route disruptions that may worsen weekend sanitation.
evidence: 9 missed collection complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (350% increase, z-score: 4.67)
Timing suggests a new operational disruption—equipment failure, staffing shortage, or route change
Related: 'Dirty Condition' complaints (185 over 90 days) remain elevated baseline, likely exacerbated by collection gaps
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to confirm whether a specific collection area or route has been disrupted this week
Interview residents on streets with repeated missed pickups—how long has this been happening?
Check if staffing or vehicle issues at the local sanitation garage are driving the spike

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints exploded to 3 THIS WEEK versus a 0.1 weekly average—a 2,300% spike—indicating either sudden illegal vending activity on beaches/boardwalk or heightened city enforcement action.
evidence: 3 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2,300% increase, z-score: 8.69)
Spike is acute and brand-new—suggests either a sudden problem or a new city crackdown initiative
Related: Real Time Enforcement complaints also spiked 700% (5 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 avg), indicating broader enforcement tempo shift
reporting_angles: Did the NYPD or Parks Enforcement Patrol launch a new vendor sweep on Coney Island boardwalk this week?
Are unlicensed food vendors or merchandise sellers operating in newly visible clusters?
Interview vendors and business improvement districts on enforcement intensity and compliance challenges

themes_detail.label: Animal Welfare & Public Health Spike
themes_detail.summary: Combined animal-related complaints (9 animals in parks last week + 7 dead animals 2 weeks ago) total 16 incidents over two weeks versus baseline of ~2.4 weekly, suggesting either wildlife population surge, inadequate animal control response, or reporting surge driven by public health concern.
evidence: Animals in parks: 9 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (554% increase, z-score: 6.26)
Dead animals: 7 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.0 weekly average (600% increase, z-score: 6.0)
Combined signal over past 2 weeks shows sustained animal control challenge, not one-off incident
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Dept on whether there's a known wildlife incursion (raccoons, coyotes) or feeding-driven aggregation near Coney Island parks
Check if dead animal removal is delayed, creating visible public health hazards
Speak with residents and park-goers on safety concerns and whether animal encounters are increasing

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street sign missing complaints surged to 4 LAST WEEK versus a 0.4 weekly baseline—a 967% spike—while broader street/sidewalk condition complaints (Root/Sewer/Sidewalk up 700%) suggest accelerating pavement and drainage infrastructure decay.
evidence: Street sign missing: 4 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% increase, z-score: 5.21)
Root/Sewer/Sidewalk condition: 3 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% increase, z-score: 5.42)
Convergent signal suggests systemic street maintenance backlog or storm/salt damage acceleration
reporting_angles: Map where missing signs and damaged sidewalks cluster—are specific neighborhoods neglected?
Interview DOT on sign replacement priorities and sidewalk repair backlog in this district
Check whether recent winter weather (salt, freeze-thaw cycles) has accelerated deterioration
